title: International Business
source_note: Grounded in standard international business theory: theories of international trade, modes of entry into foreign markets, the international monetary system, foreign exchange, regional economic integration, and multinational enterprise strategy, as taught in NUC-aligned Nigerian business administration programmes.

questions.question: International business is best defined as:
options: Commercial transactions that occur between two or more countries
Transactions that occur only within a single country's borders
The internal accounting practices of a single firm
The study of a nation's constitution
questions.correct_answer: Commercial transactions that occur between two or more countries
questions.explanation: International business covers all commercial transactions -- private and governmental -- between parties in two or more countries.

questions.question: According to Adam Smith's theory of absolute advantage, trade between two countries is beneficial when:
options: Each country specializes in producing goods it can produce more efficiently than the other
Both countries produce identical goods at identical costs
One country produces everything it needs domestically
Countries impose high tariffs on all imports
questions.correct_answer: Each country specializes in producing goods it can produce more efficiently than the other
questions.explanation: Absolute advantage theory holds that a country should specialize in and export goods it produces more efficiently than other countries, and import what it produces less efficiently.

questions.question: David Ricardo's theory of comparative advantage argues that mutually beneficial trade can occur even when:
options: One country has an absolute advantage in producing all goods
Neither country has any advantage in any good
Both countries have identical resource endowments
Trade barriers are completely eliminated
questions.correct_answer: One country has an absolute advantage in producing all goods
questions.explanation: Comparative advantage shows that a country should specialize in the good where its relative (opportunity cost) advantage is greatest, even if it is more efficient at producing everything.

questions.question: The Heckscher-Ohlin theory explains trade patterns primarily based on differences in countries':
options: Relative factor endowments, such as labor and capital
Political systems
National languages
Religious beliefs
questions.correct_answer: Relative factor endowments, such as labor and capital
questions.explanation: The Heckscher-Ohlin (factor proportions) theory predicts that countries export goods that intensively use their abundant factors of production.

questions.question: A tariff is best defined as:
options: A tax imposed by a government on imported (or occasionally exported) goods
A quota limiting the physical quantity of imports
A subsidy paid to domestic exporters
A voluntary agreement to restrict exports
questions.correct_answer: A tax imposed by a government on imported (or occasionally exported) goods
questions.explanation: Tariffs are taxes levied on goods crossing a national border, most commonly on imports, raising their price relative to domestic goods.

questions.question: A quota, as a trade barrier, restricts international trade by:
options: Limiting the physical quantity of a good that can be imported
Imposing a percentage tax on the value of imports
Subsidizing domestic producers directly
Requiring foreign firms to pay export duties
questions.correct_answer: Limiting the physical quantity of a good that can be imported
questions.explanation: Import quotas cap the volume or value of a specific good that may be imported during a given period, unlike tariffs which tax rather than restrict quantity directly.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common argument used to justify protectionism?
options: Protecting infant industries from foreign competition
Maximizing global consumer welfare
Eliminating all domestic industries
Increasing the price of exports to zero
questions.correct_answer: Protecting infant industries from foreign competition
questions.explanation: The infant industry argument holds that new domestic industries need temporary protection from established foreign competitors until they become competitive.

questions.question: Exporting as a mode of foreign market entry is generally characterized by:
options: Low risk and low control compared to foreign direct investment
The highest possible level of control over foreign operations
Mandatory establishment of a foreign subsidiary
The transfer of full ownership of production facilities abroad
questions.correct_answer: Low risk and low control compared to foreign direct investment
questions.explanation: Exporting requires relatively low resource commitment and risk but also gives the firm less control over marketing and distribution compared to direct investment.

questions.question: Licensing as an entry mode involves:
options: Granting a foreign firm the right to use intellectual property such as patents or trademarks for a fee
Directly building a factory in the foreign country
Merging with a foreign competitor
Selling goods exclusively through the firm's own domestic retail stores
questions.correct_answer: Granting a foreign firm the right to use intellectual property such as patents or trademarks for a fee
questions.explanation: Licensing allows a foreign licensee to use the licensor's proprietary technology, brand, or processes in exchange for royalty payments.

questions.question: Franchising differs from licensing mainly in that franchising typically:
options: Involves a more comprehensive package including the business model, brand, and ongoing operational support
Never involves any brand name usage
Is used exclusively for manufacturing heavy machinery
Requires no ongoing relationship between the parties
questions.correct_answer: Involves a more comprehensive package including the business model, brand, and ongoing operational support
questions.explanation: Franchising is a more extensive form of licensing that includes an entire business system, brand standards, and continued support, common in services like fast food.

questions.question: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) is best defined as:
options: An investment made by a firm to acquire a controlling ownership interest in a foreign business
The purchase of foreign stocks purely for short-term financial gain
A government grant to a foreign nation
A loan from one government to another
questions.correct_answer: An investment made by a firm to acquire a controlling ownership interest in a foreign business
questions.explanation: FDI involves establishing or acquiring a lasting management interest (typically 10% or more ownership) in an enterprise operating in a foreign country.

questions.question: A greenfield investment, as a form of FDI, involves:
options: Building entirely new operating facilities from the ground up in a foreign country
Purchasing an existing foreign company's shares
Merging two domestic firms
Licensing technology to a local partner
questions.correct_answer: Building entirely new operating facilities from the ground up in a foreign country
questions.explanation: Greenfield investment establishes a completely new operation abroad, as opposed to a brownfield investment which acquires or merges with existing facilities.

questions.question: A wholly owned subsidiary as an entry mode gives the parent firm:
options: Full ownership and control of foreign operations
Only partial ownership shared equally with a local partner
No decision-making authority over the foreign unit
Only the right to license its brand name
questions.correct_answer: Full ownership and control of foreign operations
questions.explanation: A wholly owned subsidiary is entirely owned by the parent company, giving it complete control but requiring the greatest resource commitment and risk.

questions.question: A multinational enterprise (MNE) is best described as a firm that:
options: Owns or controls value-adding activities in more than one country
Operates exclusively within its home country
Only exports goods without any foreign operations
Is owned entirely by a single foreign government
questions.correct_answer: Owns or controls value-adding activities in more than one country
questions.explanation: MNEs coordinate and control production or service activities across national borders, distinguishing them from purely domestic or export-only firms.

questions.question: The foreign exchange market is primarily where:
options: Currencies of different countries are bought and sold
Domestic stocks are traded
Government bonds are issued exclusively
Real estate transactions occur
questions.correct_answer: Currencies of different countries are bought and sold
questions.explanation: The foreign exchange (forex) market facilitates the conversion of one currency into another to support international trade and investment.

questions.question: A depreciation of a country's currency relative to another currency means that:
options: It now takes more units of the domestic currency to buy one unit of the foreign currency
It now takes fewer units of the domestic currency to buy one unit of the foreign currency
The domestic currency has been officially revalued upward by the government
Exchange rates have become completely fixed
questions.correct_answer: It now takes more units of the domestic currency to buy one unit of the foreign currency
questions.explanation: Currency depreciation means the domestic currency has weakened, so more of it is required to purchase the same amount of foreign currency.

questions.question: Under a fixed exchange rate system, a country's currency value is:
options: Pegged to another currency or a basket of currencies and maintained by the government
Allowed to float freely based purely on market supply and demand
Determined solely by private commercial banks
Irrelevant to international trade
questions.correct_answer: Pegged to another currency or a basket of currencies and maintained by the government
questions.explanation: In a fixed exchange rate regime, the government or central bank sets and defends a specific exchange rate, often through intervention.

questions.question: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) was primarily established to:
options: Promote international monetary cooperation and provide financial assistance to member countries with balance-of-payments problems
Provide long-term development loans exclusively for infrastructure projects
Set global tariff rates for all countries
Regulate the internal tax systems of member states
questions.correct_answer: Promote international monetary cooperation and provide financial assistance to member countries with balance-of-payments problems
questions.explanation: The IMF, created at Bretton Woods, oversees the international monetary system and offers financial support to countries facing balance-of-payments difficulties.

questions.question: The World Bank's primary mission is to:
options: Provide financing and advice to developing countries for development projects
Set exchange rates for all member currencies
Act as a commercial bank for individual consumers
Print currency for its member nations
questions.correct_answer: Provide financing and advice to developing countries for development projects
questions.explanation: The World Bank Group provides loans, grants, and technical assistance to developing countries to reduce poverty and support development projects.

questions.question: The World Trade Organization (WTO) primarily functions to:
options: Provide a framework for negotiating trade agreements and resolving trade disputes between member nations
Set global interest rates
Manage the foreign exchange reserves of member countries
Issue passports for international travelers
questions.correct_answer: Provide a framework for negotiating trade agreements and resolving trade disputes between member nations
questions.explanation: The WTO administers global trade rules, provides a forum for trade negotiations, and adjudicates disputes among its member countries.

questions.question: A free trade area, as a level of regional economic integration, is characterized by:
options: Elimination of tariffs among member countries while each retains its own external trade policy
A common currency shared by all member countries
Complete political union of member states
A single central bank governing all members
questions.correct_answer: Elimination of tariffs among member countries while each retains its own external trade policy
questions.explanation: In a free trade area, members remove trade barriers among themselves but each country sets its own tariffs toward non-member countries.

questions.question: A customs union differs from a free trade area primarily because a customs union additionally:
options: Adopts a common external tariff toward non-member countries
Allows completely free movement of labor and capital
Uses a single shared currency
Merges the political governments of member states
questions.correct_answer: Adopts a common external tariff toward non-member countries
questions.explanation: A customs union goes beyond a free trade area by harmonizing external tariffs that member countries apply to non-members.

questions.question: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) is an example of which form of regional economic cooperation?
options: A regional economic community aiming at economic integration among West African states
A purely military alliance with no economic function
A global body governing all world trade
A bilateral agreement between only two countries
questions.correct_answer: A regional economic community aiming at economic integration among West African states
questions.explanation: ECOWAS is a regional grouping of West African countries, including Nigeria, established to promote economic integration and cooperation in the sub-region.

questions.question: The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) primarily aims to:
options: Create a single continental market for goods and services with free movement of trade across African countries
Establish a single African currency immediately
Replace all national governments in Africa with one government
Restrict trade between African nations
questions.correct_answer: Create a single continental market for goods and services with free movement of trade across African countries
questions.explanation: AfCFTA seeks to boost intra-African trade by reducing tariffs and non-tariff barriers, creating a unified market across the continent.

questions.question: Culture, in the context of international business, is best understood as:
options: The shared values, beliefs, and norms that shape behavior within a society
A country's official exchange rate policy
The physical geography of a nation
A firm's balance sheet structure
questions.correct_answer: The shared values, beliefs, and norms that shape behavior within a society
questions.explanation: Culture encompasses the learned values, attitudes, and behavioral norms shared by members of a society, significantly influencing international business practices.

questions.question: Geert Hofstede's cultural dimensions framework is commonly used in international business to:
options: Compare and analyze cultural differences between countries that affect management practices
Calculate exchange rate fluctuations
Determine a country's GDP growth rate
Set international shipping tariffs
questions.correct_answer: Compare and analyze cultural differences between countries that affect management practices
questions.explanation: Hofstede's framework identifies dimensions such as power distance, individualism-collectivism, and uncertainty avoidance to compare national cultures relevant to business.

questions.question: 'Power distance', as one of Hofstede's cultural dimensions, refers to:
options: The extent to which less powerful members of a society accept unequal power distribution
The physical distance between a country's capital and its business districts
The exchange rate gap between two currencies
The number of trade barriers between two nations
questions.correct_answer: The extent to which less powerful members of a society accept unequal power distribution
questions.explanation: Power distance measures how much a culture accepts hierarchical, unequal distribution of power in institutions and organizations.

questions.question: Ethnocentrism in international business management refers to:
options: The belief that one's home country's practices are superior and should be applied globally
The practice of adapting fully to local host-country customs
A strategy of hiring only local nationals in every subsidiary
A neutral, unbiased view of all cultures
questions.correct_answer: The belief that one's home country's practices are superior and should be applied globally
questions.explanation: An ethnocentric orientation assumes home-country approaches are best and tends to impose them on foreign operations, often causing cultural friction.

questions.question: A polycentric staffing approach in international human resource management involves:
options: Hiring host-country nationals to manage foreign subsidiaries
Filling all key foreign management posts with home-country expatriates only
Recruiting only third-country nationals for every position
Refusing to hire any local staff
questions.correct_answer: Hiring host-country nationals to manage foreign subsidiaries
questions.explanation: A polycentric approach staffs foreign subsidiaries primarily with local (host-country) managers who understand the local market and culture.

questions.question: Political risk in international business refers to the risk that:
options: Political decisions or instability in a host country will negatively affect a firm's operations or investment
A firm's domestic sales will decline due to poor marketing
A firm's employees will resign voluntarily
Currency exchange rates will remain perfectly stable
questions.correct_answer: Political decisions or instability in a host country will negatively affect a firm's operations or investment
questions.explanation: Political risk covers threats such as expropriation, regulatory changes, civil unrest, or government instability that can harm foreign business operations.

questions.question: Expropriation, as a political risk, refers to:
options: A host government seizing a foreign firm's assets, sometimes with compensation
A firm voluntarily selling its assets to a local partner
A firm's decision to relocate its headquarters
A reduction in a country's tariff rates
questions.correct_answer: A host government seizing a foreign firm's assets, sometimes with compensation
questions.explanation: Expropriation occurs when a host government takes ownership of foreign-owned assets, which may or may not include fair compensation to the owner.

questions.question: A countertrade arrangement in international business involves:
options: Exchanging goods or services for other goods or services rather than for money
A purely cash-based export transaction
The purchase of foreign shares on a stock exchange
A government subsidy paid to importers
questions.correct_answer: Exchanging goods or services for other goods or services rather than for money
questions.explanation: Countertrade is a form of international trade in which goods or services are exchanged for other goods or services, often used when currency is scarce.

questions.question: A letter of credit used in international trade primarily serves to:
options: Guarantee payment to the exporter once specified shipping and documentary conditions are met
Replace the need for any shipping documentation
Eliminate currency exchange requirements entirely
Serve as a substitute for a business visa
questions.correct_answer: Guarantee payment to the exporter once specified shipping and documentary conditions are met
questions.explanation: A letter of credit is a bank's guarantee of payment to an exporter once the exporter presents documents proving that goods were shipped as agreed.

questions.question: Global standardization strategy in international business emphasizes:
options: Offering a largely uniform product and strategy across all markets to achieve economies of scale
Fully customizing every product for each individual national market
Selling only in the domestic market
Ignoring cost efficiencies entirely
questions.correct_answer: Offering a largely uniform product and strategy across all markets to achieve economies of scale
questions.explanation: A global standardization strategy pursues low costs through economies of scale and scope by offering standardized products worldwide with minimal local adaptation.

questions.question: A localization (multidomestic) strategy in international business focuses on:
options: Customizing products and marketing to fit the specific needs of each national market
Selling a single identical product worldwide with no adaptation
Eliminating all foreign subsidiaries
Setting one universal price for all countries
questions.correct_answer: Customizing products and marketing to fit the specific needs of each national market
questions.explanation: A localization strategy adapts products, services, and marketing approaches to local tastes and requirements, prioritizing local responsiveness over global efficiency.
